sm: President Trump said in the White House briefing room that the war with Iran is militarily, effectively over, pointing to polite talks with Tehran, though he said the naval blockade stays and military action remains an option. He said he would work with Democrats on immigration but not on amnesty, and UFC president Dana White said he does not want to be press secretary. American diplomats are leading new Russia and Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi, while Bloomberg reported leaked records suggesting about four hundred thousand Russians have died in the war. Congressman Thomas Massie is pushing an impeachment vote on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, and Hakeem Jeffries said he is a hard yes. Senators in both parties are questioning leadership, with Majority Leader John Thune scheduling elections and some Democrats cool on Chuck Schumer. The Supreme Court cleared the way for border wall construction in the Big Bend region of Texas.

Reporter Travis Kirchner in Jerusalem spoke with US Ambassador Mike Huckabee about the US and Israel alliance. Huckabee said even he was surprised when President Trump announced the end of four billion dollars a year in aid to Israel on election day. He called last week's Republican losses a bloodbath, blamed partly on far-right voters who treat America first as America only, and defended the Iran war by recalling the 1979 hostage crisis. He voiced worry about anti-Semitism from Democrats such as Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, denied that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza, and said the partnership will stay strong. The report noted that a majority of Americans now support cutting aid. The episode then began a report by Emma Eicher on California's new law requiring paid political influencers to disclose payment.

Under California's new law, which takes effect in January, influencers paid by campaigns must disclose it, and criminal, civil and administrative penalties apply, including fines up to five thousand dollars per violation. Hans von Spakovsky, a former Federal Election Commission member, backed disclosure but said criminal penalties go too far for First Amendment reasons, and that only the influencer, not the campaign, should be liable if the campaign told them to disclose. Saurav Ghosh of the Campaign Legal Center said paid posts are plain political advertising and should follow the same rules as other media, but that federal action could take years. Texas passed a similar requirement earlier this year. Mary then interviewed David Bozell of the Media Research Center, who said the group has tracked liberal media bias quantitatively since 1987, including bias by omission and guest lists on shows like The View.

Bozell said conservatives dominate cable and talk radio, but forty-eight percent of Americans get news from the big four aggregators, Apple News, Google News, MSN and Yahoo News. His group found that Apple News went ninety-nine straight days without linking to a conservative site, and he said Apple is human curated. He added that everyone has bias and the question is whether reporting is objective. A short story followed about a deer that crashed through two windows of an apartment in Appleton, Wisconsin. Then Jenny Rough reported on a six thousand eight hundred mile relay along the American Discovery Trail for the nation's 250th birthday, organized by Dave Wittsen, who earlier walked nearly the whole trail alone. The route mixes wilderness with towns, pavement and greenways, and crosses historic places like the Platte River and Lewis and Clark country.

The relay began July first at Point Reyes in California, with batons carrying a copy of the Declaration of Independence, and aims to reach Delaware by Thanksgiving. It paused in August after wildfire smoke and heat near Boulder, Utah, with the gap to be filled next spring. About two thousand people have taken part, and it just reached West Virginia. Wittsen said walking America helps people see they have more in common than media suggests. Commentator Daniel Sir then said that while Republicans Michelle Tafoya and Mike Rogers ran pro-abortion ads and lost, Democrats like Josh Turek in Iowa won by distancing themselves from wokeness, such as opposing males in female sports. He said Republicans may have been victims of their own success, and he will watch whether these Democrats hold the line. Tomorrow's show brings Washington Wednesday with Hunter Baker.
